defmodule Ledger.Money.Type do
  @moduledoc """
  An `Ash.Type` wrapping a `Ledger.Money` value. Storage type is `:map`.
  """

  use Ash.Type

  alias Ledger.Money

  @impl Ash.Type
  def storage_type(_opts), do: :map

  @impl Ash.Type
  @doc """
  Accepted inputs (same value for all):
  - nil -> nil
  - Ledger.Money struct
  - map with :currency/:amount or "currency"/"amount" keys
  - canonical string
  """
  def cast_input(nil, _), do: {:ok, nil}
  def cast_input(%Money{} = money, _), do: {:ok, money}

  def cast_input(map, _) when is_map(map) do
    with {:ok, currency} <- fetch_currency(map),
         {:ok, amount} <- fetch_amount(map) do
      Money.new(amount, currency)
    else
      err -> err
    end
  end

  def cast_input(str, _) when is_binary(str) do
    case parse_string(str) do
      %Money{} = money -> {:ok, money}
      {:error, reason, extra} -> error(reason, extra)
      {:error, reason} -> error(reason)
    end
  end

  def cast_input(_other, _), do: error(:invalid_format)

  @doc "Loading preserves round-tripped storage values, errors for anything else."
  def load(value, _opts, _context) do
    case value do
      %{"amount" => amount, "currency" => currency} when is_integer(amount) ->
        case Money.new(amount, String.to_existing_atom(currency)) do
          {:ok, money} -> {:ok, money}
          _ -> error(:invalid_format)
        end

      _ ->
        error(:invalid_format)
    end
  end

  @doc "Write to storage as a map with string keys (Jason-safe)."
  def dump_to_native(%Money{currency: currency, amount: amount}, _opts) do
    {:ok, %{"amount" => amount, "currency" => Atom.to_string(currency)}}
  end

  def dump_to_native(nil, _), do: {:ok, nil}
  def dump_to_native(_value, _), do: :error

  @impl Ash.Type
  def constraints, do: [:currencies, :min, :max, :multiple_of]

  @impl Ash.Type
  def apply_constraints(nil, _constraints, _context), do: :ok

  def apply_constraints(value, constraints, context) do
    check_order = ~w[currencies multiple_of min max]a
    check(value, constraints, check_order, context)
  end

  defp check(_value, _constraints, [], _context), do: :ok

  defp check(value, constraints, [head | tail], context) do
    case check_single(value, head, constraints, context) do
      :ok -> check(value, constraints, tail, context)
      {:error, error} -> {:error, error}
    end
  end

  defp check_single(value, :currencies, constraints, _context) do
    case Keyword.fetch(constraints, :currencies) do
      {:ok, allowed} when is_list(allowed) ->
        if value.currency in allowed,
          do: :ok,
          else: error(:currency_not_allowed, currency: value.currency)

      _ ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  defp check_single(value, :multiple_of, constraints, _context) do
    case Keyword.fetch(constraints, :multiple_of) do
      {:ok, multiple} when is_integer(multiple) and multiple > 0 ->
        if rem(value.amount, multiple) == 0,
          do: :ok,
          else: error(:not_multiple_of, multiple_of: multiple)

      _ ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  defp check_single(value, :min, constraints, _context) do
    case Keyword.fetch(constraints, :min) do
      {:ok, bound} ->
        case cast_bound(bound) do
          {:ok, %Money{currency: vc, amount: va}, %Money{currency: bc, amount: ba}} ->
            case Money.compare(value, bound) do
              :lt -> error(:below_min, min: Money.to_string(bound))
              _ -> :ok
            end

          {:error, reason} ->
            error(reason)

          {:error, reason, extra} ->
            error(reason, extra)
        end

      _ ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  defp check_single(value, :max, constraints, _context) do
    case Keyword.fetch(constraints, :max) do
      {:ok, bound} ->
        case cast_bound(bound) do
          {:ok, %Money{currency: vc, amount: va}, %Money{currency: bc, amount: ba}} ->
            case Money.compare(value, bound) do
              :gt -> error(:above_max, max: Money.to_string(bound))
              _ -> :ok
            end

          {:error, reason} ->
            error(reason)

          {:error, reason, extra) ->
            error(reason, extra)
        end

      _ ->
        :ok
    end
  end

  # --- Helpers -------------------------------------------------------------

  # Resolve currency first: atom must be supported, string upcased code.
  defp fetch_currency(map) do
    case Map.fetch(map, :currency) do
      {:ok, c} when is_atom(c) -> validate_currency(c)
      {:ok, c} when is_binary(c) -> validate_currency(String.downcase(c))
      {:ok, c} -> error(:unknown_currency, currency: c)
      :error ->
        case Map.fetch(map, "currency") do
          {:ok, c} when is_atom(c) -> validate_currency(c)
          {:ok, c} when is_binary(c) -> validate_currency(String.downcase(c))
          {:ok, c} -> error(:unknown_currency, currency: c)
          :error -> error(:invalid_format)
        end
    end
  end

  defp validate_currency(c) when is_atom(c) do
    if Money.new(0, c) == {:ok, Money.zero(c)},
      do: {:ok, c},
      else: error(:unknown_currency, currency: c)
  end

  defp validate_currency(str) when is_binary(str) do
    case Money.new(0, String.to_existing_atom(str)) do
      {:ok, money} -> {:ok, money.currency}
      _ -> error(:unknown_currency, currency: str)
    end
  rescue
    ArgumentError -> error(:unknown_currency, currency: str)
  end

  # Fetch amount: integer or string of digits with optional sign.
  defp fetch_amount(map) do
    case Map.fetch(map, :amount) do
      {:ok, a} when is_integer(a) -> {:ok, a}
      {:ok, a} when is_binary(a) -> parse_amount(a)
      {:ok, a} -> error(:invalid_format)
      :error ->
        case Map.fetch(map, "amount") do
          {:ok, a} when is_integer(a) -> {:ok, a}
          {:ok, a} when is_binary(a) -> parse_amount(a)
          {:ok, a} -> error(:invalid_format)
          :error -> error(:invalid_format)
        end
    end
  end

  # Matches "-?[0-9]+" (integer digits); rejects fraction with dot.
  defp parse_amount(str) do
    cond do
      str =~ ~r/^-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$/ -> error(:fractional_minor_units)
      str =~ ~r/^-?[0-9]+$/ -> {:ok, String.to_integer(str)}
      true -> error(:invalid_format)
    end
  end

  # Parse canonical string: uppercase code, optional sign, major units.
  # The exponent must match the number of fraction digits.
  defp parse_string(str) do
    cond do
      str =~ ~r/^-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$/ -> error(:fractional_minor_units)
      str =~ ~r/^-?[0-9]+$/ -> error(:invalid_format)
      str =~ ~r/^([a-zA-Z]+) (-?[0-9]+)(\.[0-9]+)?$/ ->
        captures = Regex.run(~r/^([a-zA-Z]+) (-?[0-9]+)(\.[0-9]+)?$/, str, capture: :all_but_first)
        [code, int, frac] = captures || ["", "0", ""]
        currency_str = String.downcase(code)

        case validate_currency(currency_str) do
          {:ok, currency} ->
            exponent = Money.exponent(currency)

            case {frac, exponent} do
              {nil, 0} -> Money.new(String.to_integer(int), currency)
              {"." <> f, ^exponent} ->
                case Money.new(parse_major(int, f), currency) do
                  {:ok, m} -> m
                  {:error, r} -> error(r)
                end
              {_other, _exp} -> error(:invalid_format)
            end

          {:error, reason, extra} -> error(reason, extra)
          {:error, reason} -> error(reason)
        end
      true -> error(:invalid_format)
    end
  end

  # Parse major + frac into minor units with exact integer arithmetic.
  defp parse_major(int, frac) do
    sign = if String.starts_with?(int, "-"), do: -1, else: 1
    abs_int = String.to_integer(lstrip_sign(int))
    abs_frac = String.to_integer(frac)
    exponent = String.length(frac)

    # amount = sign * (abs_int * 10^exponent + abs_frac)
    10 ** exponent * abs_int + abs_frac |> Kernel.*(sign)
  end

  defp lstrip_sign("-" <> rest), do: rest
  defp lstrip_sign(s), do: s

  # Cast bound into a Money value (or return error).
  defp cast_bound(bound) do
    case cast_input(bound, []) do
      {:ok, %Money{} = money} -> {:ok, money, money}
      error -> error
    end
  end

  defp error(message, reason, extra), do: {:error, [message: message, reason: reason] ++ extra}
  defp error(message, reason), do: {:error, [message: message, reason: reason]}
  defp error(reason), do: error(default_message(reason), reason)

  defp default_message(:unknown_currency), do: "unknown currency"
  defp default_message(:fractional_minor_units), do: "amount must be a whole number of minor units"
  defp default_message(:invalid_format), do: "invalid money format"
  defp default_message(:currency_not_allowed), do: "currency is not allowed"
  defp default_message(:not_multiple_of), do: "must be a multiple of %{multiple_of} minor units"
  defp default_message(:below_min), do: "must be greater than or equal to %{min}"
  defp default_message(:above_min), do: "must be greater than or equal to %{min}" # unused
  defp default_message(:above_max), do: "must be less than or equal to %{max}"
  defp default_message(:currency_mismatch), do: "cannot compare money in different currencies"
end

    aggregate :paid_minor, :payments, :amount_minor, kind: :sum, default: 0
  end

  calculations do
    calculate :total, Ledger.Money.Type, &calculate_total/2
    calculate :balance, Ledger.Money.Type, &calculate_balance/2

    case Ledger.Money.sum((invoice.adjustments || []) ++ [invoice.subtotal], invoice.subtotal.currency) do
      {:ok, money} -> money
      _ -> invoice.subtotal
    end
  end

  def calculate_balance(invoice, _context) do
    paid = (invoice.payments || [])
           |> Enum.reduce(Ledger.Money.zero(invoice.subtotal.currency), fn p, acc ->

    do: Ash.Changeset.set_attribute_of_nil(changeset, :adjustments, [])

defmodule Ash.Type.NewType do
  @moduledoc """
  Allows defining a new type that is the combination of an existing type and custom constraints

  A subtle difference between this type and its supertype (one that will almost certainly not matter
  in any case) is that we use the `apply_constraints` logic of the underlying type in the same step
  as `cast_input`. We do this because new types like these are, generally speaking, considering the constraint
  application as part of the core type. Other types, if you simply do `Ash.Type.cast_input/3` you will not be
  also applying their constraints.

  ## Options

  - `:subtype_of` - The type that this new type is a subtype of.
  - `:constraints` - The constraints that this new type uses for the underlying type.
  - `:lazy_init?` - If true, the `init/1` function will be called at runtime instead of compile time.
    Allows for recursive types.

  For Example:

  ```elixir
  defmodule MyApp.Types.SSN do
    use Ash.Type.NewType, subtype_of: :string, constraints: [match: ~r/regex for ssn/]
  end

  defmodule MyApp.Types.Metadata do
    use Ash.Type.NewType, subtype_of: :union, constraints: [types: [
      foo: [...],
      bar: [...]
    ]]
  end
  ```

  @doc "Whether or not the type is lazy initialized (so needs to be initialized when fetching constraints)"
  @callback lazy_init?() :: boolean()
  @doc "Returns the underlying subtype constraints"
  @callback subtype_constraints() :: Keyword.t()
  @doc "Returns the modified NewType constraints"

  @doc "Returns true if the corresponding type is an Ash.Type.NewType"
  @spec new_type?(Ash.Type.t()) :: boolean
  def new_type?({:array, type}), do: new_type?(type)
  def new_type?(type), do: Spark.implements_behaviour?(type, __MODULE__)

  @doc "Returns the type that the given newtype is a subtype of"
  @spec subtype_of(t()) :: Ash.Type.t()
  def subtype_of({:array, type}), do: {:array, subtype_of(type)}

  def subtype_of(type) do

      subtype_of = type.subtype_of()

      if new_type?(subtype_of) do
        subtype_of(subtype_of)
      else
        subtype_of
      end
    else
      type
    end
  end
